svg.text: Teske-type hidden Weil descent: the three ingredients, by field type

E over F_{q^n}; weak set of size q^{n-δ}; isogeny class of size q^{n/2}; margin a = δ - n/2 (exponents in units of log q, constants dropped). Tags: [T] source or proof, [E] exact count of this round, [H] heuristic.

g.text: 1. Non-class-invariant weakness
GHS genus depends on the model (b, or the branch set
of a degree-2 function), not on the trace. [T: GHS 2002 §1]
Anomalous, MOV, group order: class invariants, cannot be hidden.
2. Transfer along the secret isogeny
E_pb → E_s (degree coprime to r), then conorm-norm
E_s(F_{q^n}) → Jac(C)(F_q). [T: Teske 2006; Hess 2004 Thm 7]
Owner's cost: index calculus on genus g, exponent 2 - 2/g [H].
3. Sparse inside the isogeny class
Auditor walks the class: q^{min(δ, n/2)} steps [H].
a > 0: hidden member not findable below rho.
a < 0: whole field weak for every covered class (MTW).
Prime fields F_p
No proper subfield: no Weil restriction,
no descent. [T: GHS 2002 §5]
Same-field covers C → E of genus g ≥ 2:
Jac(C)(F_p) has size p^g, index calculus
Base change to F_{p^k} then descend:
the group stays of size p; same bound. [T]
Non-class-invariant weaknesses known:
none with an exponential gain. [O]
Ingredients 1 and 3 absent.
No Teske-type variant via descent.
Binary fields F_{2^{nl}} (n odd, d = ord_n(2))
Weak set: Ord_b | F, |{b}| = q^{deg F}, m = deg F + [x+1 ∤ F]. [T: MMT 2002]
gGHS (Hess): b = (αβ)^2, genus 2^t - 2^{t-r} - 2^{t-s} + 1, δ = n + 1 - r - s. [T]
n = 7 (Teske's field, N = 161):
type I g = 7, δ = 4, a = +0.5 → 11.5 bits: hidden [E]
type II g = 8, δ = 3, a = -0.5 → walk 2^69 < rho 2^80 [E]
gGHS g = 7, δ = 2, a = -1.5: half of all classes covered [T: MT 2006]
n = 3, 5: δ ≤ 1, every curve descends (weak fields) [T: MTW 2004]
n = 15: the public n = 5 sub-descent already beats rho.
Prime n (NIST): m ≥ d + 1 with d large: no descent [T: Menezes–Qu]
All three ingredients present only for n ∈ {7 (type I), 15, 21, 31, …}.
Auditor's answer: reject composite N, or audit every N = n·l (ec_trapdoor.rs).
Isogeny-class coverage at toy N: ghs_class_coverage.rs; Yee 2016 (F_{2^150}).
Odd characteristic F_{q^n} (Kummer descents)
Weak set: branch orbit type (m, r), genus 1 + 2^{m-2}(r-4), δ = n + 3 - r. [T/E]
n = 2 (r=5, g=2): δ = 0, no gain over rho [T: Scholten]
n = 3 (r=5, g=3): δ = 1, a = -0.5: weak field via walk [T: JV 2012]
n = 4 (g=5): r=5 type δ = 2, a = 0; r=6 types δ = 1, a = -1 [E]
n = 5 (r=5, g=5): δ = 3, a = +0.5: the one hidden regime [E]
n = 6 (r=6, g=9): δ = 3, a = 0: borderline [E; JV App. C]
n = 7 (r=7, g=7): δ = 3, a = -0.5: weak field via walk [E]
prime n ≥ 11: genus ≥ 1793, nothing descends [T: Diem 2003]
Other associations (ingredient 1 widened):
Jac(C) ~ Res(E) by L-polynomial (Tate): a cover of some degree.
Census: most Res-shaped genus-3 hyperelliptic Jacobians are NOT
GHS compositums [E]; Tian 2020: (ℓ,ℓ,ℓ)-isogenies for prime order [T].
Hidden regime exists at n = 5 only (genus 5 over F_q).
Auditor's answer for F_{q^5}: test every branch type of period 5 (Part B).
Trace-zero / decomposition attacks are class-invariant: not hideable, not trapdoors.

svg.text: research/teske_variants_field_types_20261018 · exponents only; every "hidden" or "weak" label is a formula on exact invariants, not a measured attack.
